NavigationService.phobosnav_help_status_:
phobosnav: status | settings | fly [km] | dock | stop | resume | cruise <m/s> | arrivalspeed <m/s> | arrival <km> | defaults | torch on/off | forget | spawn. Defaults explicitly resets this console’s preferences; forget clears its saved flight. N2: rendezvous [km] | follow [km] | spawnpursuit. N3: firetarget | weapons <1–9> | volley | fireweapon | aimweapon | autoaim | engage | ceasefire | nativefire. Engage requires N3 and a separately selected qualified target, including during manual flight. Cease retains offensive Hold; nativefire releases it and may resume native autofire. Rendezvous/Follow match motion. Native N3 spawn: spawn PhobosNavModFireControl.
phobosnav approachdock — approach the cleared target and hand over to terminal RCS docking.
Audio: phobosnav watch | unwatch | cue-volume. Engage Approach/Rendezvous before watching.

Hub.placement_notice: Polaris Flight Hub: open the navigation console's layout Edit menu and place one tall hub (one column, four rows). Move or hide the old left-column instruments first; keep the native map, sensors, warnings and specialist panels accessible. Existing compact positions are not enlarged. N1 and N2 share one hub.
Hub.help:
Navigation: Approach stops at your chosen separation. Dock uses RCS for the final approach. Approach & Dock keeps the selected target and ports, approaches a point 1 km beyond hull clearance, matches motion, then checks the docking approach. If already inside that point, it checks docking directly. Keep the navigation console open for final clamps. Clearance, fees and port fit still apply.

Closing speed is positive when moving towards the target, negative when moving away. Relative speed includes sideways drift. A dash means no current reading. Alignment is the difference between ship headings, not a measurement of the ports themselves.

N2 enables Rendezvous and Follow. N3 enables Fire, including during manual flight or coasting. Select a separate fire target, weapon group and volley limit; lift the cover and Engage. Auto Aim is a separate choice. Cease Fire stops aiming and holds offensive fire while Follow can continue. Return to Native releases the hold and may allow normal automatic firing again. Weapons still need power, ammunition, aim, range, clear firing arcs and any required missile lock. Braking takes priority. If the guarded switch cannot be displayed, Engage is blocked.

Systems controls disengage automation before changing reactor flow or thrust. The reactor must be ready; the thrust limiter and no-wake restrictions still apply. The hub cannot start a cold reactor. Stored energy means energy connected to this console, not total ship generation. Use reactor and specialist panels for startup and fault finding.

Disengage cuts commanded thrust; the ship keeps moving and spinning. Combined docking and pursuit pause after loading. Resume checks the original module, target and ports. Changing pages never issues a command.

If standard autopilot, station-keeping or held thrust blocks engagement, Disengage clears those controls on this ship and sets torch cycle to zero. Reactor power stays on. Other AI or flight mods must release control themselves. Resume needs a saved paused flight; Cease Fire needs active flight or fire control. N1 alone does not enable pursuit or weapons.

FCS.returned: Native control restored; native automatic firing may resume.
FCS.aim_unavailable: Auto Aim needs free RCS control or compatible Auto Nav flight. Docking, departure and industrial movement take priority.
FCS.migration: N2 now supplies pursuit only. Install Phobos' Asterel N3 Polaris Fire Control System for weapons and optional RCS aiming. Existing flight bindings are preserved.
FCS.pursuit_help:
Rendezvous matches motion and finishes. Follow maintains separation. Both require N2.

Combat requires N2 + N3. Select a fire target and Use for aim on the Fire tab first. Enter Combat uses the speed and separation above, suspends the previous flight, and starts range matching and aiming. Engage weapons separately.

Braking, traffic avoidance and torch manoeuvres take priority over weapon facing. Cease Fire stops aiming and firing while range matching continues. Leave Combat to change movement settings; Resume the previous flight explicitly.
FCS.help:
Select a tracked fire target and one weapon group. Volleys (1–9) counts successful firing batches: each batch fires the weapons ready at that moment, not one projectile per weapon. Lift the cover to Engage. With Auto Aim off, weapons can operate while you fly manually.

Auto Aim permits RCS turning while coasting, or requests a heading during Approach, Rendezvous, Follow or Combat. Choose a weapon with Weapon > and Use for aim. When aiming is active, pilot thrust or turning cancels aiming and firing. Braking and clearance take priority.

Cease Fire or the end of a volley order stops Auto Aim and keeps offensive fire on hold. Follow and Combat range matching can continue. Return to Native exits Combat and releases the hold and may allow normal automatic firing again. Defensive PDCs and deliberate manual fire still work normally. Choose an installed group from the picker. If FCS holds the old group, confirm its return to native control; the new group stays on hold. Left-click Volleys to increase; right-click to decrease. Both wrap between 1 and 9. Switched-off and damaged weapons remain listed but cannot fire.

Loading a save keeps fire on hold. It does not restore targets, firing permission, remaining volleys or aiming. Missing or stale readings mean unavailable. Missiles need permission for automatic fire and a full lock; decoys are excluded. Hits, intact boarding and crew survival are never guaranteed. Use the map, sensors and specialist weapon settings as usual.

Needs a usable sensor track and permitted, ready weapons. Loading a save keeps fire on hold; it never rearms the system.

Departure.reserve: Departure needs a tracked ship or station and enough RCS fuel for at least 42 m/s of speed change before disconnecting.
